newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airlines to get info on HK airport fees - official.
newsitem.headline: Airlines to get info on HK airport fees - official.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said on Friday it should be able to provide airlines with more information on charges at the territory's new Chek Lap Kok airport by the end of April.

"I expect that will happen," chief executive Henry Townsend told reporters in response to a question on whether information on the charges would be made available at the next meeting of the authority and the airlines in late April.
Airlines are negotiating with the authority on the charges they will pay at Chek Lap Kok, which is scheduled to open in April 1998.
Townsend earlier told a business luncheon that the authority was proposing to nearly double the charges at the new airport compared to those at existing Kai Tak airport.
The charges include landing fees, parking fees and passenger terminal fees, he said.

Antony Tyler, director of corporate development of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, refused to comment on the Airport Authority proposal, but said the airline would like to have the breakdown on the charges to evaluate whether they were fair.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has said its research showed there was no need for higher charges.

The authority has said the charges would be fair and reasonable, allow it to meet its obligation to operate on prudent commercial principles, would reflect the "user pays" principle and avoid the need for public subsidy.
